Article Title: India’s first hydrogen-powered train completes over 1,200 km trials, saves 3,200 litres of diesel; onboard fuel cells generate electricity, emit only water vapour
Article Text:
File photo: Jind-Sonipat Hydrogen Train

Train generates electricity using hydrogen fuel cells

Developed indigenously by Indian Railways

Dedicated hydrogen storage facility set up at Jind

Multiple safety systems incorporated

Independent hydrogen leak detection systems

Heat, flame and smoke sensors

Automatic emergency shut-off systems

Continuous ventilation

Compliance with international safety standards

Mandatory technical validations before operations

Delhi trials planned next

India's first hydrogen-powered train has travelled more than 1,200 kilometres since it was flagged off on July 17, with Railways saying the project has already saved over 3,200 litres of diesel during trial operations between Jind and Sonipat in Haryana.According to a railway ministry press release, the successful trial runs have paved the way for the next phase of testing, with operations on the Delhi route expected to begin soon.Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the country's first hydrogen-powered train from Jind under the Centre's Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative.Unlike conventional diesel locomotives, the hydrogen train produces electricity onboard through a chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen inside fuel cells, according to the Railway Ministry.The electricity generated powers the train's motors, while water vapour is the only by-product released during the process.Because there is no combustion, the train produces no smoke or tailpipe carbon emissions, making it one of the cleanest forms of rail propulsion currently available, the ministry said.The hydrogen train has been developed as an indigenous project by Indian Railways.According to the railway ministry, the train consists of 10 passenger coaches and two Hydrogen Driving Power Cars that together generate 2,400 kW of power.The propulsion system is supported by lithium iron phosphate batteries along with hydrogen cylinders.Railways minister Ashwini Vaishnaw described the project as a landmark achievement, saying the propulsion system and related technology were developed within India.The project has also led to the establishment of Indian Railways' first dedicated hydrogen storage and refuelling facility at Jind.The railway ministry said green hydrogen is stored at pressures of up to 500 bar and dispensed at 350 bar. The facility has a storage capacity of around 3,000 kilograms of hydrogen to support regular train operations.According to the ministry, the train has been equipped with several safety features, including:The ministry said these measures are intended to ensure the safe operation of hydrogen-powered trains under Indian conditions.Following the successful operations between Jind and Sonipat, Indian Railways plans to begin trial runs on the Delhi route.According to the railway ministry, the project aims to establish an indigenous hydrogen rail ecosystem while supporting the country's transition towards zero-emission rail transport.Officials said the initiative could lay the foundation for wider deployment of hydrogen-powered trains across India in the future.
Article Summary: India's first hydrogen-powered train has travelled more than 1,200 kilometres since it was flagged off on July 17. The project has already saved over 3,200 litres of diesel during trial operations between Jind and Sonipat in Haryana. Indian Railways plans to begin trial runs on the Delhi route soon.

Article Title: Rs 1 crore in aid, website linking lawyers to protesters: How CJP plans to fight cases across India
Article Text:
CJP announces legal aid

Sibal pledges Rs 1 crore aid

CJP seeks written agreement

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Monday announced plans to launch a website to raise public donations for a legal aid fund and connect lawyers with protesters facing legal action after the 37-day NEET agitation.The announcement came amid the party's allegations that protesters were being detained and cases were being filed despite assurances from the Centre that no action would be taken after the agitation ended on July 25.Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the organisation had sought legal advice from senior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal before and after calling off the protests.Das said the party feared that participants could face legal action once the movement ended."We were in constant touch with Kapil ji and had sought legal guidance. When we called off the protest on the 25th, we apprehended that in the future, once the movement subsided or the momentum of the protest waned, the government might start targeting individuals. This is a very credible apprehension, as the same playbook has been observed in other major protests where individuals were singled out and implicated in false cases," he said.He said the organisation had been providing legal and medical support to students since the beginning of the agitation and was now expanding that network across states.Kapil Sibal announced financial support for the initiative and said he would contribute Rs 1 crore to the legal aid fund. He also appealed to lawyers across the country to represent protesters facing cases."We don't want any action against those who sat in protest. It was an organic protest. Often governments want no dissent. Wherever there were peaceful protests and wherever protestors were targeted, they will create a website. I will give Rs 1 crore. I appeal to lawyers to aid us so that wherever in India there are trials our lawyers will help protestors who are being tried," Sibal said.Earlier in the day, the CJP accused the Centre of violating the understanding reached when the protest was called off.In a post on X, CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka alleged that students had been arrested in Bihar and West Bengal, while volunteers in Delhi and Uttar Pradesh were being detained or harassed.The party demanded that FIRs against protesters be withdrawn, detained students be released and a written agreement on legal protections be shared by Tuesday. It warned that it would resume protests if these demands were not met.Ranka said the CJP had submitted a draft agreement to Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and was waiting for the government to share the final version after legal consultations.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announces plans to launch a website to raise public donations for a legal aid fund and connect lawyers with protesters facing legal action. Announcement came amid the party's allegations that protesters were being detained and cases were being filed despite assurances from the Centre that no action would be taken.

Article Title: Govt mulls PM Surya Ghar 2.0 with battery storage, shared rooftop solar
Article Text:
Representational image

NEW DELHI: As the number of households benefiting from rooftop solar installations under the Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG:MBY) nears 50 lakh, govt has begun deliberations to accelerate adoption and enhance the scheme's impact in its second phase.The ministry of new and renewable energy (MNRE) held a stakeholder consultation on Thursday, acknowledging the scheme's success in creating demand and establishing residential rooftop solar as a national market. It also identified the next set of challenges, including battery storage, grid integration, discom readiness, consumer access, asset performance, financing, quality assurance and long-term market sustainability.Launched on Feb 13, 2024, with a financial outlay of Rs 75,021 crore, the current phase of PMSG:MBY aims to install rooftop solar systems in one crore households by March 2027. So far, more than 40 lakh installations have been completed, benefiting over 48 lakh households.At the brainstorming session chaired by MNRE joint secretary JVN Subramanyam, ministry officials and industry stakeholders discussed changes that could shape PM Surya Ghar 2.0.One proposal is to ensure long-term maintenance and service support for consumers. Officials noted that many homeowners are unable to get repairs or warranty services because vendors that installed their systems have shut down or exited the business. The next phase may therefore include stricter maintenance obligations and a mechanism to guarantee electricity generation over the life of the system.The scheme may also be expanded to apartment residents and households without suitable rooftops through group and virtual net metering, allowing multiple consumers to benefit from a shared solar installation instead of individual rooftop systems.Battery energy storage systems (BESS) also figured prominently in the discussions. While batteries can store excess daytime solar power for use after sunset, they remain expensive. An official said batteries were deliberately kept out of the current scheme as they could have added to the cost and created an access barrier. With rooftop solar installations increasing rapidly and the need to better manage power during solar and non-solar hours, the role of BESS now requires fresh evaluation.The ministry plans to study whether battery storage should be deployed at the household, neighbourhood transformer or utility level before deciding the most suitable model.To improve transparency, govt may also consider digital monitoring of rooftop solar systems, while stressing the need to improve installation quality, standardise equipment and simplify financing to keep rooftop solar affordable and reliable.Officials said the suggestions will be be examined before a detailed policy paper is prepared for PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana 2.0.
Article Summary: PMSG:MBY aims to install rooftop solar systems in one crore households by March 2027. So far, more than 40 lakh installations have been completed, benefiting over 48 lakh households. The scheme may also be expanded to apartment residents and households without suitable rooftops through group and virtual net metering.

Article Title: INS Sudarshini departs Boston for Portugal after participating in US's 250th Independence Day anniversary celebrations
Article Text:
The ministry said INS Sudarshini has now set sail for Ponta Delgada, Azores (Portugal)

NEW DELHI: Indian Navy Sailing Ship Sudarshini has set sail for Portugal, wrapping up its month-long visit to the US to participate in the celebrations of the country’s 250th anniversary of independence.“The Indian Naval Ship Sudarshini, a sail training vessel of the Indian Navy, departed Boston, US, on July 25 as part of the ongoing Lokayana 26 voyage,” a defence ministry statement said in Delhi. “Representing India at the historic SAIL250 celebrations, the IndianNavy’s sail training ship showcased the nation’s rich maritime heritage while deepening maritime partnerships,” the Navy said on X on Sunday.The ministry said INS Sudarshini has now set sail for Ponta Delgada, Azores (Portugal), continuing its journey as a beacon of India’s maritime strength, professionalism, and goodwill on the global stage.INS Sudarshini arrived at Boston on Sunday after her successful participation in the Sail4th 250 celebrations at New York. The ship took part in the Grand Parade of Sails, marking the commencement of Sail Boston 2026, the Ministry of Defence said. Raghuram Sastry, consul general of India in Boston, embarked on INS Sudarshini for the Grand Parade of Sails and the ship’s ceremonial entry into Boston.Joining an international fleet of over 60 tall ships from over 20 nations, INS Sudarshini is representing India as a maritime ambassador of goodwill during her ongoing Lokayan 2026 transoceanic expedition.INS Sudarshini is a three-masted barque, 54 metres long and has 20 sails, 7.5 km of rope and 1.5 km of steel wire rope. The ship's sails have a total area of approximately 1,035 square metres (11,140 sq ft). Capable of operations under sail or power, and with a complement of five officers, 31 sailors, and 30 cadets embarked for training, the ship can remain at sea for at least 20 days at a time.
Article Summary: INS Sudarshini has now set sail for Ponta Delgada, Azores (Portugal) The ship took part in the Grand Parade of Sails, marking the commencement of Sail Boston 2026. The ship is a three-masted barque, 54 metres long and has 20 sails.

Article Title: Delay in paying land compensation proves costly for Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
Supreme Court ordered TN to either return 970 acres of land it had acquired in 2009-10 for the establishment of industries or pay compensation to landowners

NEW DELHI: Already facing a fiscal crisis, Tamil Nadu Monday found itself in a difficult situation when Supreme Court ordered it to either return 970 acres of land it had acquired in 2009-10 for establishment of industries or pay compensation to landowners at the market rate as of January 1, 2014.Appearing for State Industries Promotion Corporation of Tamil Nadu (SIPCOT), senior advocates A M Singhvi and Prashanto Sen told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that government is ready to pay Rs 21 crore as per the earlier procedure. However, senior advocate Arvind Nayar, appearing for a landowner's trust, said though the acquisition process began in 2009-10, no award was passed, thereby rendering the process incomplete.Nayar said Tamil Nadu government has been sitting on the land for nearly two decades and not paid a penny as compensation to landowners. "The Madras HC found that since the central law on payment of compensation for acquisition of land had come into force, the cutoff date would be Jan 1, 2014." Singhvi said if Jan 1, 2014, was made the cutoff date, the compensation amount would increase from Rs 21 crore to more than Rs 180 crore and impose a heavy burden on the state's finances.But Supreme Court said, "When you acquire land, you must be prepared to pay adequate compensation to the landowners. Why should they suffer because of government's inaction? You wanted land for industries, so you pay compensation at market rate."Singhvi then requested Supreme Court to limit the relief of higher compensation to the 10 petitioners who had approached the court. But the bench said if the state finds it difficult to pay compensation as directed, it would have to return the land to owners in six weeks.
Article Summary: Supreme Court ordered TN to either return 970 acres of land it had acquired in 2009-10 for the establishment of industries or pay compensation to landowners at the market rate as of January 1, 2014. Appearing for State Industries Promotion Corporation of Tamil Nadu (SIPCOT), senior advocates A M Singhvi and Prashanto Sen told a bench of CJI Surya Kant.

Article Title: Supreme Court: Insolvency shield is for firm, not promoters
Article Text:
IBC is to facilitate the resolution process and not to eclipse the statutory remedies

Moratorium to preserve assets of corporate for resolution: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Promoters of real estate companies use pending insolvency proceedings as a shield to protect themselves in court cases filed by homebuyers for not giving possession of flats, but Supreme Court on Monday clarified that a moratorium against the corporate debtor does not give protection to promoters and directors, and proceedings can continue against them.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta quashed an order passed by the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission by which a consumer complaint against promoters and directors of a Bengaluru-based real estate company was stayed in view of insolvency proceedings against the company. The court allowed the plea of homebuyers who challenged the NCDRC order.Section 14 of Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code provides that once insolvency process begins and a moratorium is declared, the continuation of pending suits and proceedings against the corporate debtor, including execution proceedings, comes to an automatic halt. The object of this moratorium is to preserve the assets of the corporate debtor during the insolvency resolution proceedings and to facilitate an orderly resolution.Explaining the provision, the bench said it was not open either to the adjudicating authority or the court to enlarge its ambit beyond what the statute contemplated, and a plain reading of the provision made it clear that the moratorium operated against the corporate debtor alone.“No other category, whether it be any subsidiary company, any managers/directors, personal guarantors etc, can be added to it unless specifically provided,” it said.Homebuyers had moved SC through advocate Chandrachur Bhattacharya, contending that promoters of the company could not claim protection of the moratorium. Accepting their plea, the court said the protective sweep of a moratorium must remain within the four walls as carved out by the statute.“It ought not be expanded in a manner that stultifies remedies envisaged under the Consumer Protection Act, unless expressly provided. Code is to facilitate the resolution process and not to eclipse the statutory remedies,” the bench said while reviving the proceedings against promoters of Mantri Technology Constellation Pvt Ltd.“In the present case, respondent no. 1 (company) alone is the corporate debtor against whom the CIRP has been initiated. No independent moratorium or independent protection operates in favour of respondent nos. 2 to 7 (promoters and directors). In the absence of any legal bar against continuation of proceedings qua the said respondents, NCDRC was not justified in rejecting appellants’ prayer to proceed with the complaint against the rest of the respondents,” the bench said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court clarifies that a moratorium against the corporate debtor does not give protection to promoters and directors. Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta quashed an order passed by the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. The court allowed the plea of homebuyers who challenged the NCDRC order.

Article Title: Need out-of-box thinking to plug paper leaks, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
Structural reform must

NEW DELHI: As government informed Supreme Court that a high-powered committee has been formed for education reform, the court said Monday that some "out-of-box thinking" was needed to address problems faced by the sector, including the recurring problem of paper leaks.Appearing before a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe, solicitor general Tushar Mehta told Supreme Court the PM has announced a high-powered task force headed by ex-executive chairperson of Infosys, Nandan Nilekani , to recommend structural reforms. The court was hearing a PIL seeking that the medical entrance be shifted to a computer-based test.Mehta told the bench that the court was scheduled to take up the NEET paper leak petition on Aug 3 and pleaded that this petition be tagged and heard with them.Deferring the hearing to August 3, the bench said govt needed to examine what additional safeguard was required to conduct the online exam and ensure data security.Amid protests by the youth against paper leaks and demands that govt fix accountability and bring reforms, Supreme Court on July 24 said the system's ad hocism was "troubling", which could not be allowed to go on, and assured that it would "tread the extra mile" to fix the problems and make NEET foolproof."We are focusing on institutionalisation. This is the most important." said the bench, adding that it will keep monitoring the process.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says some "out-of-box thinking" was needed to address problems faced by the sector. The court was hearing a PIL seeking that the medical entrance be shifted to a computer-based test. The bench said govt needed to examine what additional safeguard was required to conduct the online exam and ensure data security.

Article Title: CJP's win fuels call by 'E20 Janta Party' for no-ethanol option
Article Text:
Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association have announced a march to Parliament against E20 petrol on Aug 4

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think consumers should have the option to buy 100% petrol? Yes, consumers should have a choice No, the current policy is enough 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Inspired by Cockroach Janta Party's campaign over the NEET paper leak that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister, a new outfit - E20 Janta Party - has stepped into the ring, demanding consumers be given the option of buying 100% petrol and seeking the resignation of road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari.The campaign has found support among transporters, with Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association announcing a march to Parliament against E20 petrol on August 4.The association alleged that the ethanol-blending policy has reduced fuel efficiency, increased maintenance costs and affected engine performance, particularly in older vehicles.Also Read: Ethanol blended fuel damaged vehicles of people, claims Maharashtra Congress chief E20 Janta Party, which gained more than 25,000 followers on X in a few hours Sunday, said it was not seeking subsidies, free fuel or withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol, but only demanding that consumers be given the choice to buy the fuel they want.It also demanded transparent fuel labelling so consumers knew what they were buying, publication of data on the costs, benefits and impact of fuel blends, and independent studies on mileage, engine performance, emissions and maintenance costs.Although ethanol-free 100-octane premium petrol has long been available in the country, it is sold only at select fuel stations and costs Rs 169 per litre, compared with Rs 102.12 per litre for standard E20 fuel (in Delhi).Minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi told Parliament last week that govt had not received "widespread or substantiated" complaints on ethanol-blended petrol affecting vehicle performance.
Article Summary: E20 Janta Party has stepped into the ring, demanding consumers be given the option of buying 100% petrol. The campaign has found support among transporters, with Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association announcing a march to Parliament.

Article Title: MBBS admissions: NMC puts focus on ability, not disability
Article Text:
National Medical Commission on Monday issued new guidelines

NEW DELHI: Students with benchmark disabilities seeking admission to MBBS courses will now undergo an individual assessment of their functional abilities to determine whether they can acquire the essential competencies required for the course with reasonable accommodation. The National Medical Commission (NMC) on Monday issued new guidelines requiring medical boards to evaluate each candidate's functional ability rather than relying solely on the type or extent of disability.Under the new framework, designated Medical Assessment Boards will carry out an individual assessment of every candidate. The guidelines state that applicants cannot be declared ineligible solely on the basis of their diagnosis or the percentage of benchmark disability. Instead, boards must assess a candidate's functional abilities, the essential competencies required under the Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME) curriculum, and whether reasonable accommodation can enable them to complete the course."After the Supreme Court's constant follow-up and directions, the NMC has finally amended its interim guidelines and issued revised guidelines for MBBS admissions of students with disabilities.The biggest change is the shift from assessing eligibility on the basis of the percentage of disability to evaluating functional competency. Clinical accommodations are reasonable modifications that enable medical students with benchmark disability to participate in clinical training and patient care without compromising academic standards or patient safety," said Prof Satendra Singh, Coordinator of the Enabling Unit at UCMS and GTB Hospital.The guidelines also require medical boards to consider assistive devices, adaptive technology, communication support and other reasonable accommodations before arriving at a decision. Any finding of ineligibility must be supported by objective medical and functional evidence and recorded in writing.While emphasising inclusion, the NMC has said patient safety will remain an important consideration. However, it has directed that decisions should be based on objective medical and functional assessment rather than assumptions or stereotypes about disability.The regulator has also introduced a uniform assessment process, standard eligibility certificates and an appeal mechanism for candidates aggrieved by the decision of the Medical Assessment Board. The guidelines have been issued under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, read with the Graduate Medical Education Regulations, 2023, and come into force with immediate effect.
Article Summary: The National Medical Commission (NMC) on Monday issued new guidelines requiring medical boards to evaluate each candidate's functional ability. Under the new framework, designated Medical Assessment Boards will carry out an individual assessment of every candidate. The guidelines state that applicants cannot be declared ineligible solely on the basis of their diagnosis or the percentage of benchmark disability.

Article Title: NMC asks medical colleges to set up support units for students with disabilities
Article Text:
National Medical Commission (TNN)

NEW DELHI: Every medical college regulated by the National Medical Commission (NMC) will now have to set up an "Enabling Unit" for students with benchmark disabilities, providing a single point of contact for reasonable accommodation, academic and clinical support, and a barrier-free learning environment. The move follows the NMC's new guidelines on assessing students with benchmark disabilities for MBBS admissions.In a circular issued on Monday, the NMC directed all medical colleges and institutions under its ambit to constitute the Enabling Units in compliance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, and recent Supreme Court directions aimed at ensuring inclusive medical education.According to the circular, the Enabling Unit will function as the single point of contact for students with benchmark disabilities. It will facilitate access to reasonable accommodation, academic and clinical support measures, and barrier-free access within the institution. The unit will also receive and address requests for disability-specific accommodations during the course of study, including clinical training and internship."Clinical accommodations are reasonable modifications that enable medical students with disabilities to participate in clinical training and patient care without compromising academic standards or patient safety," said Prof Satendra Singh, coordinator of the Enabling Unit at UCMS and GTB hospital.He added that the Enabling Units are not a matter of charity but a mandatory requirement under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, aimed at providing a level playing field for students with disabilities.Medical colleges have also been asked to publicise the availability of the Enabling Unit through their websites and notice boards, coordinate with Disability Assessment Boards, faculty and hospital administration, and maintain records of requests and accommodations while ensuring confidentiality and non-discrimination.The NMC has directed all medical colleges to ensure that the Enabling Unit is functional, easily accessible and adequately publicised to promote an inclusive educational environment for students with benchmark disabilities. The circular has been issued with the approval of the competent authority.
Article Summary: Every medical college regulated by the National Medical Commission will now have to set up an "Enabling Unit" The move follows the NMC's new guidelines on assessing students with benchmark disabilities for MBBS admissions. According to the circular, the Enabling Unit will function as the single point of contact for students with benchmarks disabilities.

Article Title: Ayodhya Ram mandir donation row: On Supreme Court suggestion, temple SIT to include a forensic auditor
Article Text:
During the last hearing, the bench had warned petitioners against politicising the issue

NEW DELHI: The UP government on Monday immediately accepted Supreme Court's suggestion for inclusion of a chartered accountant having expertise in forensic audit in the three-member SIT, constituted on the Supreme Court's July 20 order to investigate alleged embezzlement of donations to Ayodhya Ram mandir managed by Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.As soon as a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought to know the UP govt's view on inclusion of a chartered accountant having expertise in forensic audit in the SIT headed by IGP Kiran S, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said, "Without taking instructions from the govt, I am assuring the court that such an expert will be drafted into the SIT."The bench said, "We want an expeditious, fair and transparent investigation into all aspects of allegations relating to alleged misappropriation of donation funds for the temple managed by the trust."Appearing for a PIL petitioner, advocate Devadatt Kamat said since there were allegations of siphoning out of donations meant for temple construction from across the country, the trust should be asked to upload all receipts of donations on its website."This will help devotees identify whether their donations for construction of the temple and thereafter have been accounted for or not," Kamat said and requested the court to entrust supervision of the SIT probe to a retired Supreme Court judge.The SG objected and said, "We must trust the Supreme Court and three honourable judges who are monitoring it."The CJI-led bench turned down Kamat's request and said, "When we are monitoring the probe being carried out by the SIT, there is no need of any supervision by a retired judge. The SIT will transparently investigate all aspects of allegations relating to siphoning of funds." It asked the SIT to submit a probe status report in two weeks.During the last hearing, the bench had warned petitioners against politicising the issue and assured that there would be fair, impartial, transparent and expeditious investigation by the SIT. Supreme Court said if the SIT experienced any impediment from any quarter in carrying out the investigation, it should approach Supreme Court without loss of time.
Article Summary: The UP government on Monday immediately accepted Supreme Court's suggestion for inclusion of a chartered accountant having expertise in forensic audit in the three-member SIT. The SIT is constituted on the Supreme court's July 20 order to investigate alleged embezzlement of donations to Ayodhya Ram mandir managed by Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.

Article Title: 47 GW battery storage, 23 GW pumped storage projects in pipeline
Article Text:
Representative AI-generated image

NEW DELHI: India has nearly 47 GW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity at various stages of development as the country ramps up storage infrastructure to support rapid expansion of renewable energy and meet rising electricity demand, power ministry informed Parliament Monday.As of June 30, nearly 16 GW of BESS capacity was under construction, about 12 GW awarded, while another 19 GW is at the tendering stage, MoS for power Shripad Yesso Naik said in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. On the pumped storage front, 16 GW of projects are under construction, while another 7 GW has received concurrence and is awaiting construction.As per National Electricity Plan (Generation), India is projected to require 47 GW of battery energy storage capacity and 27 GW of pumped storage capacity by 2031-32. The minister said large-scale deployment of storage systems will be critical for integrating renewable energy, meeting peak electricity demand and ensuring grid reliability.The minister also said India will require investments of about Rs 4.8 lakh crore in energy storage infrastructure by 2031-32 to support the growing share of renewable energy in the power mix. Of the total investment, about Rs 3.5 lakh crore is estimated for battery energy storage systems and Rs 1.3 lakh crore for pumped storage projects.The storage push comes alongside an aggressive capacity addition programme. Since April 2023, 21 GW of thermal power capacity has been commissioned, while 48 GW, including 4.8 GW of stressed projects, is under construction. Contracts have also been awarded for another 16 GW of coal- and lignite-based capacity.On the renewable side, 148 GW of capacity is under construction, while another 48 GW is at various stages of planning and targeted for completion by 2029-30.The ministry said India’s installed power generation capacity is projected to reach 874 GW by 2031-32, with states preparing 10-year resource adequacy plans to ensure generation capacity remains ahead of projected demand.
Article Summary: India has nearly 47 GW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity at various stages of development. The country is ramping up storage infrastructure to support rapid expansion of renewable energy. As of June 30, nearly 16 GW of BESS capacity was under construction, about 12 GW awarded, while another 19 GW is at the tendering stage.

Article Title: NHAI wins major arbitration, Rs 3,177-cr claim cut to Rs 46 cr
Article Text:
The NHAI’s wins major arbitration case

NEW DELHI: NHAI, in a recent arbitration case, has got an arbitration order in its favour, rejecting the majority of claims – against the claim of Rs 3,177 crore by a contractor; the arbitral tribunal awarded only Rs 46 crore to settle the case.In an official statement, the highways authority said that the arbitration case involved 151-km Bareilly-Sitapur BOT (Toll) highway project in Uttar Pradesh.The dispute arose after NHAI terminated the concession agreement with Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL), a company promoted by Era Infra Engineering Ltd, in May 2019. The concessionaire had sought compensation of around Rs 3,177 crore through 30 claims before a three-member arbitral tribunal.In its award, the tribunal allowed only three claims worth about Rs 46 crore, along with applicable interest, while rejecting the overwhelming majority of the claims. The tribunal also upheld the validity of the “supplementary agreement” signed on March 30, 2015, and ruled that delays in the project were concurrent, weakening the concessionaire's case.NHAI had filed counterclaims relating to financial losses and public inconvenience caused by the stalled project.Although these counterclaims were not accepted, the authority successfully defended itself against the bulk of the concessionaire's claims, substantially reducing its potential financial exposure.The latest ruling adds to a series of arbitration successes for NHAI this year. In June, it secured an award of Rs 1,202 crore in the Tumkur-Chitradurga six-laning project in Karnataka. Earlier, arbitration in the Panipat-Jalandhar highway project involving claims exceeding Rs 8,000 crore was settled at Rs 819.96 crore in NHAI's favour. In another case relating to the Kamrej-Chalthan section of NH-48 in Gujarat, claims of Rs 174.5 crore were reduced to just Rs 54 lakh.toied
Article Summary: The dispute arose after NHAI terminated the concession agreement with Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL), a company promoted by Era Infra Engineering Ltd. The concessionaire had sought compensation of around Rs 3,177 crore through 30 claims before a three-member arbitral tribunal. The tribunal allowed only three claims worth about Rs 46 crore, along with applicable interest.

Article Title: Bihar's dairy push: New plant in Nalanda to boost farmer incomes, create jobs
Article Text:
Bihar bets big on value-added dairy, launches 20 MTPD curd and lassi plant in Nalanda

COMFED outlines expansion roadmap

Bihar laid the foundation stone for a modern 20 metric tonne per day curd and lassi processing plant in Nalanda, on Monday. This marks a significant step in the state's ambition to emerge as a stronger player in India's fast-growing dairy industry.Chief minister Samrat Choudhary laid the foundation for the facility at the Biharsharif Dairy Project, which is expected to substantially enhance the production capacity of COMFED's flagship brand Sudha. The expansion aims to meet rising demand for value-added dairy products while preparing the brand to compete in global markets as India strengthens its position as the world's largest milk producer.The new facility is expected to encourage further investments in dairy processing, reinforce Bihar's efforts to build a robust dairy value chain, and deliver higher returns to farmers. It also positions the state to capitalise on India's growing competitive advantage in the global dairy sector.The expansion is closely aligned with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of 'Sahkar Se Samriddhi' (Prosperity through Cooperation) and the objectives of White Revolution 2.0, launched by Union home and cooperation minister Amit Shah. As India seeks to strengthen its dairy cooperative movement and enhance the global footprint of Indian dairy products, Sudha is steadily evolving from a trusted regional brand into a nationally respected and globally competitive dairy brand.Towards this objective, COMFED is expanding village-level dairy cooperative societies, increasing milk procurement, and promoting greater participation of women in the dairy economy.Addressing the gathering, chief minister Choudhary commended COMFED and Bihar's dairy cooperatives for their contribution to the state's rural economy and expressed confidence that Sudha would evolve into a globally competitive dairy brand. "Sudha represents much more than a dairy brand. It is the backbone of the livelihoods, self-reliance and aspirations of millions of dairy farmers across Bihar," he said.Through its extensive cooperative network, Sudha has ensured that producers receive fair remuneration while strengthening the rural economy and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities.Shirsat Kapil Ashok, Managing Director of COMFED, highlighted the federation's achievements during the first 100 days of the present government, including the formation of more than 2,500 new dairy cooperative societies across Bihar. This has resulted in an increase of over 300,000 litres of milk procurement per day compared to the previous year.Outlining the roadmap for the next 100 days, Ashok said COMFED would expand initiatives such as Sudha Sakhi and the Prime Minister's Veterinary Medicine Centres, while implementing key livestock breed improvement projects. These include a proposed Semen Station in Lakhisarai and an AITI Centre in Munger, aimed at improving cattle genetics and productivity.The chief minister distributed deep freezers to 300 retailers to strengthen Sudha's frozen products distribution network and flagged off a specially designed vehicle for transporting sick and infirm livestock.
Article Summary: Bihar laid the foundation stone for a modern 20 metric tonne per day curd and lassi processing plant in Nalanda. This marks a significant step in the state's ambition to emerge as a stronger player in India's fast-growing dairy industry. The expansion aims to meet rising demand for value-added dairy products.

Article Title: 'MPs sleeping, need wake-up call': Delhi transport bodies plan Parliament march on August 4 against E20 fuel

NEW DELHI: Delhi-based transport bodies are likely to hold a protest march to Parliament, demanding the withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol.The planned protest would be led by the Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association along with other groups."We are planning to hold a protest march to Parliament on August 4 against ethanol-blended petrol and demand its withdrawal. We want to give a wake-up call to MPs who are sleeping on the issue, as vehicle problems linked to ethanol blending are being reported from across the country," Sanjay Samrat, president of the Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association, told PTI.He also distanced the protest call from the so-called "E-20 Janta Party" and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The CJP, an online satirical outfit, had on July 20 led a march to Parliament seeking the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET (UG) paper leak controversy, which resulted in clashes between protesters and police."We do not want to make this a political issue and are not associated with any 'E-20 Janta Party', Cockroach Janta Party or any other political party," Samrat added, referring to the online campaign against E20 fuel, which is a blend of 20% ethanol and 80% petrol.According to Harish Sabharwal, national president of the All India Motor Transport Congress, the association was protesting against the government’s move to make E20 fuel the only option available to consumers."Ethanol-blended petrol should not be forced upon commuters; there should be a choice. Currently, no option is being provided. We are supporting the protest march to Parliament, but the association has not given any call for a strike as of now," Sabharwal stated.The protest announcement comes days after the launch of the "E-20 Janata Party," an online movement formed along the lines of the CJP, which has gained a large following on Instagram and X.The E20 ethanol-blending policy has been at the centre of a major controversy, with concerns raised over reduced vehicle mileage, possible engine wear and alleged conflicts of interest.The government has defended the programme, ruling out any immediate plans to increase ethanol blending beyond 20% and maintaining that the fuel is safe, cleaner and beneficial for farmers.
Article Summary: Delhi-based transport bodies are likely to hold a protest march to Parliament, demanding the withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol. The government has defended the programme, ruling out any immediate plans to increase ethanol blending.

Article Title: Ram Temple donation 'theft' case: SC tells SIT to submit status report within 2 weeks

Article Title: Kapil Sibal challenges anti-defection law: SC to examine tenth schedule merger rule
Article Text:
Kapil Sibal challenges tenth schedule: SC issues notice to Centre on anti-defection law

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the current political climate in India impacted significantly by defections? Yes, very much No, not really I don't know 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(with inputs from agencies)

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the Centre's response to a plea filed by independent Rajya Sabha leader and senior advocate Kapil Sibal challenging the interpretation of the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution that allows legislators to avoid disqualification under the anti-defection law by merging their political party with another party.A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe issued notice to the Centre on Sibal's plea and observed that several issues raised in the matter may require consideration by Parliament.Sibal argued that the issue has 'huge repercussions on our polity', pointing out that the provision could allow a minority party to become a majority or a majority party to become a minority.The bench observed that the Tenth Schedule, which governs defection by lawmakers, was enacted by Parliament and said it was for the legislature to devise an appropriate mechanism.Sibal also informed the court that a similar matter concerning the defection of MLAs in Goa was pending before the Supreme Court. The bench subsequently tagged his plea with the Goa matter.Sibal has filed the plea in his personal capacity and sought reconsideration of the interpretation of Paragraph 4 of the Tenth Schedule, which deals with disqualification in cases of merger.The plea seeks clarity on whether the existing interpretation permits the composition of Parliament and state legislatures to change through the merger provision without attracting disqualification under the anti-defection law.Sibal had on July 22 sought an urgent hearing of his plea, arguing that the matter concerns the manner in which the composition of Parliament can change under the existing interpretation of the Tenth Schedule.The plea has been filed against the backdrop of recent instances of legislators switching parties by invoking the merger provision under the anti-defection law. It refers to MPs from the Aam Aadmi Party, Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) joining the BJP and other political parties.The Tenth Schedule was introduced through the Constitution (Fifty-Second Amendment) Act, 1985, to curb political defections by elected representatives. Paragraph 4 provides an exception to disqualification where a political party merges with another party and the required conditions under the provision are met.
Article Summary: Supreme Court issues notice to Centre on Kapil Sibal's plea on anti-defection law. Sibal is challenging the interpretation of the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution. The provision allows legislators to avoid disqualification by merging their party with another party.

Article Title: 1993 Mumbai blasts case: SC reserves order on convict Abu Salem's plea for premature release
Article Text:
1993 Mumbai blasts case: SC reserves order on Abu Salem's plea for premature release after 25 years in jail

CBI seeks payment of Rs 16.51 lakh fine

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe justice was served in the handling of the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts case? Yes, the convictions were fair. No, there are still many unresolved issues. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday reserved its order on a plea filed by 1993 Mumbai serial blasts convict Abu Salem seeking premature release from his life sentence on the ground that he has completed 25 years in prison.Appearing for Salem, senior counsel argued that the prison authorities had failed to give him the benefit of the period he spent in custody as an undertrial, despite a specific direction from the special TADA court."Despite the categorical direction by the TADA court that I have to be given complete set-off for the undertrial period, the jail authorities are not giving me that benefit," Salem’s counsel submitted, ANI reported.The plea is linked to the terms under which Salem was extradited from Portugal. Earlier, the Supreme Court had declined to grant him interim relief and allowed him to approach the Bombay high court to examine his claim and calculate the period of imprisonment he had undergone in light of the conditions attached to his extradition.Salem was convicted in the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts case and is serving a life sentence.He has argued that, under the extradition terms, he completed 25 years of imprisonment on December 24, 2024.In his petition before the Bombay high court, Salem calculated his custody period by combining nearly 11 years and 10 months as an undertrial, nearly 10 years as a convict and more than three years of remission for good conduct. The High Court had earlier listed his plea after a special TADA court rejected his request for release.Meanwhile, the CBI has told the special TADA court that Salem must pay fines imposed in two earlier convictions before the expiry of the 25-year period applicable to his incarceration.The agency said Salem must deposit a total fine of Rs 16.51 lakh with the court registry before the completion of the stipulated period. According to the CBI, failure to pay the amount by October 12, 2030 would make Salem liable to serve the alternative default sentences prescribed by the court.Salem, who is lodged at Nashik Road Central Prison, had approached the special TADA court seeking clarity on whether he was required to pay the fines or undergo the additional sentence prescribed in case of non-payment.The CBI said the fine was not optional and that the court could direct Salem to deposit the amount in accordance with the prescribed procedure.The issue arose from fines imposed in two cases, including the murder of businessman Pradip Jain and the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts case. The CBI's response came after Salem sought directions to the prison authorities on the payment of the fines and the consequences of non-payment.Salem was extradited from Portugal in 2005 after authorities there agreed to his transfer subject to certain conditions, including restrictions on the length of his imprisonment. His case has since involved repeated legal proceedings over how his custody period should be calculated and whether the extradition terms entitle him to release after 25 years.
Article Summary: Abu Salem was convicted in the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts case and is serving a life sentence. He has argued that, under the extradition terms, he completed 25 years of imprisonment on December 24, 2024. The CBI has told the special TADA court that Salem must pay fines imposed in two earlier convictions.

Article Title: CPWD deploys 3D printing to fast-track defence construction in border areas
Article Text:
CPWD deploys 3D printing to fast-track defence construction in border areas

NEW DELHI: For the first time, Centre’s construction agency, the Central Public Works Department CPWD ), has built a watch tower (forward duty point) for the armed forces in Jammu using 3D printing construction technology in just 45 days.The project is expected to pave the way for much faster construction of such critical defence infrastructure in border areas. Conventional construction of these structures typically takes more than a year because of difficult terrain and logistical challenges.3D printing in building construction is a technology that uses a large, computer-controlled machine to build a house or other structure by laying down material, usually a special type of concrete, one layer at a time, much like a regular 3D printer makes plastic objects. Instead of workers building walls brick by brick, the printer follows a digital design to create the structure automatically, making construction faster, more accurate and less wasteful.CPWD officials said the project aimed to demonstrate the feasibility of Concrete 3D Printing Technology for rapid and efficient construction in high-security and remote locations and it was done successfully. The scope of work was a ground-plus-one storeyed building and it encompassed end-to-end delivery, including design development, procurement, construction, and commissioning of the facility with all essential services such as water supply, sanitary systems, and internal electrical installations.“Despite challenges such as restricted site access, security protocols, and logistical constraints, the project was completed successfully. The use of 3D printing technology significantly enhanced construction speed, precision, and resource efficiency, making this project a benchmark for future defense infrastructure initiatives,” an official said.
Article Summary: 3D printing in building construction is a technology that uses a large, computer-controlled machine to build a house or other structure by laying down material, usually a special type of concrete, one layer at a time. Instead of workers building walls brick by brick, the printer follows a digital design to create the structure automatically.

Article Title: Assam floods: Visuals show submerged villages, lakhs affected as death toll rises to 68

still affected.Although the flood situation has started improving and waters are receding in several areas, the death toll has climbed to 68 after two more people died in Charaideo.The Dhansiri (South) at Numaligarh was the only river still flowing above the danger level.Nearly 48,742 hectares of crop area also remained submerged.Relief and rehabilitation efforts continued across the difficulties faced by people in affected areas.The latest situation comes as rescue, relief and rehabilitation efforts continue across the state.Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Sunday described the flood situation as "very serious", saying the Centre and the state government were working together on relief and rescue operations.Sonowal said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had been closely monitoring the situation since the floods began and had remained in touch with Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma.The NDRF and SDRF are continuing rescue and relief operations, while a high-level inter-ministerial team has arrived to speak to affected people and assess the situation.Singer Papon, who hails from Assam, has appealed to people in India and abroad to come forward and support those way they could.

Article Text:

BHOPAL: Now boarding — Khajuraho Airport into top customer-ranking slot, without any flights.The airport in the Madhya Pradesh town — recently ranked India's top airport in the Airports Authority of India's latest Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) — has produced a surprising result: it has no commercial flights operating during July and Aug. The outcome has sent ripples through the aviation industry, prompting questions about the criteria of the AAI survey.Even when it had services, the scene was lacklustre: only two flights operated from the airport, connecting Delhi and Varanasi. Both have now been discontinued.The full-fledged airport, whose terminal was completed in the late 1960s and which reportedly saw its first flight in 1978, outscored larger and busier peers in the biannual passenger survey. The accolade was announced as the airport's tarmac lies quiet through the monsoon."Flights from here usually go to Delhi and Varanasi, but there are none since July 1," airport director Santosh Singh told TOI.Asked why services were suspended, Singh offered a forward-looking estimate rather than a detailed explanation, saying flights to Delhi and Varanasi are expected to restart in Oct.AAI's Customer Satisfaction Index is based on biannual surveys conducted by independent agencies to ensure objectivity.Passengers evaluate 33 core parameters — ranging from ground transport and parking to Wi-Fi and food outlets — along with additional questions on hygiene and cleanliness. Scores are combined into a composite rating out of five, officials said."In practice, this means airports with intermittent or seasonal operations can still achieve high satisfaction if facilities, cleanliness and staff conduct meet traveller expectations," said Rahul Gupta, an air traveller.The result prompted wry reactions from locals who noted the irony of an airport winning top honours while its runways see a seasonal lull. Others, however, welcomed the recognition."We are proud," said Khajuraho resident Mani Ram, pointing to the well-maintained terminal and courteous staff cited in passenger feedback.Bhopal's Raja Bhoj Airport finished third in the rankings.
Article Summary: Khajuraho Airport in Madhya Pradesh was recently ranked India's top airport in the Airports Authority of India's latest Customer Satisfaction Index. The accolade was announced as the airport's tarmac lies quiet through the monsoon. Bhopal's Raja Bhoj Airport finished third in the rankings.
